Content: Alejandro Sánchez-Salvador (Alejandro Sánchez) is a Data Scientist with a background in biology, bioinformatics and biostatistics. He spent more than 4 years in research at the Severo Ochoa Centre for Molecular Biology (CBM, CSIC-UAM, Madrid) and the University of Konstanz (Germany), working with terabytes of sequencing data, building reproducible data pipelines and contributing to 3 peer-reviewed publications (2 as first author). He holds a Master in Data Science & AI (Nuclio Digital School, 2025) and an MSc in Bioinformatics & Biostatistics (UOC-UB). He combines scientific rigour and biomedical domain knowledge with machine learning, analytics, BI dashboards and generative AI, and he ships products end to end: he built and deployed Sextant IA (https://sextantia.eu), an LLM-powered web app live in production. Since October 2026 he works as a freelance bioinformatics expert at Mercor, creating material to train and evaluate AI models.

Alejandro is looking for a full-time role in data and AI. His main focus is Pharma, Health and Life Sciences (Data Scientist, Bioinformatics or Computational Biology Data Scientist, Clinical/Biomedical Data Analyst, Real-World Data analyst, AI/ML Engineer), where he wants to apply machine learning, statistics and generative AI to biomedical, clinical and genomic data. He is also open to Data Scientist and Data Analyst roles in other industries (retail, finance, tech), where his forecasting, BI and dashboarding experience applies directly. He is based in Madrid (Spain) and open to remote, hybrid or on-site work in Spain and the rest of Europe, including relocation. He currently works as a freelancer at Mercor, so his start date is flexible.

Chronological overview: BSc in Biology, Universidad de Salamanca (2013-2017). MSc in Microbiology, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (2017-2018). Science & English tutor (2018-2020). MSc in Bioinformatics & Biostatistics, UOC-UB (2019-2022). Biotech Researcher, University of Konstanz, Germany (April 2020 - January 2022). Bioinformatics Researcher, CBM Severo Ochoa (CSIC-UAM), Madrid (September 2022 - July 2025). Online Data Analyst, Telus International AI (March 2025 - June 2025). Master in Data Science & AI, Nuclio Digital School (May 2025 - December 2025). Freelance bioinformatics expert (Writer, contractor) at Mercor (October 2026 - present).

Outside of data and coding, Alejandro loves spending time in nature and travelling to discover new cultures. He is a big fan of ancient history and often visits museums and ancient ruins on his trips (an interest that also inspired his travel planner, Sextant IA). At home he enjoys reading, cinema, and action, strategy and resource-management video games.

Since October 2026 Alejandro works remotely for Mercor as a freelance contractor (official position: Writer), acting as a bioinformatics expert. He writes expert-level bioinformatics and data analysis problems with worked solutions, which are used to train and evaluate AI models (LLMs) for a Mercor client. The project is confidential: if asked for details (client, project name, models, tasks or tools), politely explain that he cannot share them and do not speculate. This role builds on his earlier AI evaluation work at Telus International AI.

From September 2022 to July 2025 Alejandro worked as a Bioinformatics Researcher in Madrid, Spain, in a group studying the genome of the parasite Leishmania donovani. He led the computational side of multi-omics projects: he designed automated ETL pipelines in Python, R and Bash to process and integrate Ribo-Seq, RNA-seq and mass-spectrometry proteomics data, replacing manual processing, and optimised workloads with GNU Parallel across local machines and HPC. With proteogenomics he refined the genome annotation and identified new protein-coding sequences. He also ran differential expression analyses (DESeq2), whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and genome assembly projects that are not yet published, took part in the group's project decisions, and rescued a compromised Oxford Nanopore (ONT) dataset with a hybrid correction strategy using Illumina data. He ran the statistical analysis behind 3 peer-reviewed papers (2 as first author), was the group's main data contact for principal investigators and lab teams, and supervised about 5 students and technicians.

From March 2025 to June 2025 Alejandro worked part-time and remotely as an Online Data Analyst (AI & ML evaluation) for Telus International AI. He evaluated search engine results and AI model outputs against strict, detailed quality guidelines, producing human-feedback labels and 'ground truth' data used to improve the accuracy of search algorithms and machine learning models (RLHF-style human evaluation).

From April 2020 to January 2022 Alejandro worked as a Biotech Researcher in environmental transcriptomics at the University of Konstanz, Germany (AG Kroth). He ran a project end to end, from experimental design and work with bioreactors to data analysis: he managed the full data lifecycle of environmental algae samples, performed de novo transcriptome assembly and functional annotation on High-Performance Computing (HPC) clusters with Slurm, and applied multivariate statistics in R. He supervised 3 BSc/MSc students in data collection and statistical analysis in R and Excel. He used German daily at work during these two years.

From 2018 to 2020 Alejandro worked as a Science and English tutor, both at a private academy and freelance, teaching primary, secondary and upper-secondary students. This experience shaped his communication skills, patience and ability to break down complex technical concepts for non-technical audiences.

Alejandro completed a Master in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at Nuclio Digital School (May-December 2025, online). The programme covered Python, SQL, machine learning, deep learning and BI tools. His capstone project was DSMarket, an end-to-end retail demand forecasting system (see Projects).

Alejandro completed an MSc in Bioinformatics and Biostatistics at the Universitat Oberta de Catalunya together with the Universitat de Barcelona (UOC-UB, 2019-2022, online). It covered algorithms for high-dimensional data, R programming and biostatistics. His master's thesis was a differential analysis of dinoflagellate transcriptomes across nutrition modes: he built an end-to-end pipeline from raw public RNA-Seq data, with quality control (FastQC), trimming (Trimmomatic), contamination filtering (Bowtie2), de novo assembly (Trinity), functional annotation (EnTAP, KEGG, GO terms), completeness assessment (BUSCO) and phylogenetic trees, all automated in Linux/Bash.

Alejandro completed an MSc in Microbiology at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (2017-2018). His master's thesis at CBM Severo Ochoa (January-September 2018) studied the polymerase domain (PolDom) of bacterial Ligase D, involved in NHEJ DNA repair. He designed nucleotide insertion assays, quantified SDS-PAGE gels with ImageJ and fitted Michaelis-Menten kinetics in GraphPad Prism. He showed that PolDom preferentially inserts RNA nucleotides and tolerates mismatches, suggesting that under severe stress the cell favours fast, error-prone repair over leaving lethal double-strand breaks. This work was published in Biomolecules (2020), with Alejandro as first author.

Alejandro completed a BSc in Biology at Universidad de Salamanca (2013-2017). His bachelor's thesis at CIALE studied how a genetically modified Trichoderma fungus (a plant symbiont) affects tomato defences against the pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He measured defence-hormone gene expression with qPCR and analysed leaf infection rates statistically, showing that the symbiont improved the plant's defences.

DSMarket was Alejandro's capstone project for the Master in Data Science & AI (2025): an end-to-end retail demand forecasting system. He forecast weekly unit sales for about 30,000 item-store time series (3,049 products across 10 stores in 3 US cities, 6.7 million rows covering 5 years). He engineered price, calendar, weather, holiday/event and lag features, and segmented products with K-Means on sales level, price, seasonality and price elasticity. He compared Lasso regression and XGBoost with time-series cross-validation and Optuna hyperparameter tuning. The final Lasso model beat a naive last-week baseline by 10% in RMSE and 13% in WMAPE on a held-out 9-week test set; he chose Lasso over XGBoost because it was more stable in multi-week recursive forecasts and much cheaper to run. He delivered sales, revenue and demand forecasts by region, store, department and product segment in an interactive Power BI dashboard. Tools: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, XGBoost, Optuna, SQL, Power BI.

Topic: Sextant IA (AI Travel Planner, in production)
Content: Sextant IA is Alejandro's own project, live in production at https://sextantia.eu. It is an AI travel planner: an LLM-orchestrated backend with a Django frontend turns each traveller's preferences into a complete itinerary. The pipeline works in stages: it shortlists places based on the destination and the user's interests, lets the user choose activities and set dietary restrictions, builds a day-by-day skeleton, and then generates each day in parallel, enriching every location with cultural and historical context. Alejandro designed, built, deployed and maintains it end to end (architecture, prompt engineering, REST APIs, deployment). It runs on his own Oracle Cloud server behind an Nginx reverse proxy with HTTPS, and every change to the main branch is deployed automatically. It is a personal project, not institutional employment, and shows his ability to ship AI products to real users.

Alejandro built an interactive R Shiny dashboard for exploring a synthetic (simulated) clinical trial dataset of 500 patients in three arms (Placebo, Drug A, Drug B). Users can filter by treatment and gender, see KPI value boxes (number of patients, average follow-up biomarker level), an interactive ggplot2/plotly boxplot of biomarker response by treatment, and a scatter plot of baseline biomarker versus age built as a reusable Shiny module, plus a raw-data tab. It uses shinydashboard, dplyr and custom CSS, and is deployed on shinyapps.io: https://asansal.shinyapps.io/Clinical_Data_Dashboard/. All data are simulated and do not represent real patients.

Alejandro publishes interactive dashboards on Tableau Public (https://public.tableau.com/app/profile/alejandro.sanchez2642/vizzes). Health & science: Visceral Leishmaniasis map and cases per year (WHO data); Cutaneous Leishmaniasis map and cases per year (WHO data); Cutaneous Leishmaniasis endemic status by country and year; R&D&I spending in Spain 2023. Business & analytics: E-commerce retention and customer value analysis (RFM, cohorts); Daikibo manufacturing telemetry (an extended Deloitte job simulation); Market concentration monitor, 'Magnificent 7' vs S&P 500 (data pulled with Python and yfinance); Corporate equity monitor on gender pay gap and parity; NovaTech capital allocation Sankey flow. They are also shown in the Tableau section of his portfolio website.

Alejandro's portfolio website (https://asansal.com) is itself a project: a multilingual (Spanish, English, German) Streamlit single-page app with a chatbot powered by Google Gemini that answers from his own knowledge base (this document). It is hosted on a Linux server on Oracle Cloud that he set up himself (Python virtual environment, systemd service) and is deployed automatically with a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline over SSH on every push to main. Source code: https://github.com/asansal/Personal_Website

Alejandro and his team won 2nd prize at a no-code automation hackathon in Madrid. They built a smart parking assistant with Woztell and Make: the chatbot took the user's live location and car licence plate, checked the car's environmental label against local parking rules, and either confirmed that parking was allowed or recommended the nearest legal car park.

Topic: Why move from research to Data Science & AI?
Content: As a researcher, Alejandro learned that a result only counts if it is reproducible, and he found that data science and AI were the best tools to answer complex biological questions at scale. He does not want to leave science behind: he wants to bring the same rigour, plus machine learning and generative AI, to Pharma, Health and Life Sciences, where data-driven decisions directly affect patients and research. Because he has also built and deployed products end to end (Sextant IA, his portfolio website), he can take an analysis or a model all the way to production.

Topic: What has been his biggest technical challenge?
Content: During a transcriptomics project, Alejandro faced a badly compromised dataset caused by an expired Oxford Nanopore (ONT) sequencing flow cell. Instead of discarding the experiment, he designed a hybrid rescue strategy that used high-accuracy Illumina reads to correct the long-read transcriptome, and the project was saved.

Topic: Why is he targeting the DACH and Nordic regions?
Content: Alejandro identifies strongly with the professional culture of Central and Northern Europe. Having lived and worked in Germany (Konstanz), he values the work-life balance, the commitment to sustainability and nature, and the strong life-sciences and technology ecosystems in these regions. He is equally interested in opportunities in Spain.

Alejandro's salary expectations are flexible and depend on the location, cost of living and the full benefits package. He aims for the market rate for a Data Scientist or Data Analyst with his hybrid scientific and technical profile in each location. For specific figures, please contact him directly.
